points.heading: Plants
points.summary: Identify and name common wild and garden plants and trees, and describe the parts of flowering plants and trees.

points.heading: Animals, including humans
points.summary: Identify and compare fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals, what they eat, and name the parts of the human body and the senses.

points.heading: Everyday materials
points.summary: Tell an object from the material it is made of, and describe and compare the simple physical properties of materials.

points.heading: Seasonal changes
points.summary: Observe changes across the four seasons, and the weather and day length in each.

points.heading: Working scientifically
points.summary: Ask simple questions, observe closely with simple equipment and carry out simple tests to answer them.

points.heading: Living things and their habitats
points.summary: Tell living, dead and never-alive things apart, match animals to their habitats and microhabitats, and describe simple food chains.

points.heading: Plants
points.summary: Describe how seeds and bulbs grow into mature plants, and what plants need to grow and stay healthy.

points.heading: Animals, including humans
points.summary: Notice that animals have offspring that grow into adults, and describe what animals and humans need to survive and stay healthy.

points.heading: Uses of everyday materials
points.summary: Compare how suitable materials are for particular uses, and how squashing, bending, twisting and stretching change solid objects.

points.heading: Working scientifically
points.summary: Observe closely with simple equipment, perform simple tests and use observations to answer questions.

points.heading: Plants
points.summary: Identify the jobs of the parts of flowering plants, and explore the part flowers play in the life cycle.

points.heading: Animals, including humans
points.summary: Know that animals need the right nutrition from what they eat, and that some animals have skeletons and muscles for support, protection and movement.

points.heading: Rocks
points.summary: Compare and group rocks by their properties, describe how fossils are formed, and know that soils are made from rocks and organic matter.

points.heading: Light
points.summary: Recognise that we need light to see, that light is reflected from surfaces, and how shadows form and change size.

points.heading: Forces and magnets
points.summary: Compare how things move on different surfaces, group materials as magnetic or not, and predict whether magnets attract or repel.

points.heading: Working scientifically
points.summary: Set up simple practical enquiries and fair tests, and record findings to draw simple conclusions.

points.heading: Living things and their habitats
points.summary: Group living things in a variety of ways, use classification keys, and recognise that changing environments can pose dangers to living things.

points.heading: Animals, including humans
points.summary: Describe the digestive system and the types of teeth and their jobs, and construct food chains with producers, predators and prey.

points.heading: States of matter
points.summary: Compare solids, liquids and gases, the temperatures at which they change state, and the part evaporation and condensation play in the water cycle.

points.heading: Sound
points.summary: Know how sounds are made by vibrations, how they travel to the ear, and how pitch and volume change.

points.heading: Electricity
points.summary: Identify common appliances that run on electricity, build simple series circuits, and know common conductors and insulators.

points.heading: Working scientifically
points.summary: Plan fair tests, take accurate measurements with thermometers and data loggers, and report findings.

points.heading: Living things and their habitats
points.summary: Describe the differences in the life cycles of mammals, amphibians, insects and birds, and how plants and animals reproduce.

points.heading: Animals, including humans
points.summary: Describe the changes as humans develop to old age.

points.heading: Properties and changes of materials
points.summary: Compare and group materials by their properties, separate mixtures, and tell reversible changes from irreversible ones.

points.heading: Earth and space
points.summary: Describe how the Earth and planets move around the Sun, how the Moon moves around the Earth, and how day and night happen.

points.heading: Forces
points.summary: Explain gravity, air resistance, water resistance and friction, and how levers, pulleys and gears let a smaller force have a greater effect.

points.heading: Working scientifically
points.summary: Plan different kinds of enquiry, control variables and take repeat readings when appropriate.

points.heading: Living things and their habitats
points.summary: Classify living things into broad groups by their observable characteristics, including micro-organisms, plants and animals.

points.heading: Animals, including humans
points.summary: Name the main parts of the circulatory system and their jobs, and the effects of diet, exercise, drugs and lifestyle on the body.

points.heading: Evolution and inheritance
points.summary: Know that fossils tell us about living things long ago, that offspring vary from their parents, and how living things are adapted to their environment.

points.heading: Light
points.summary: Explain that light travels in straight lines, how we see objects, and why shadows have the same shape as the objects that cast them.

points.heading: Electricity
points.summary: Explain how the number and voltage of cells affect a circuit, and use recognised symbols in circuit diagrams.

points.heading: Working scientifically
points.summary: Plan enquiries that control variables, measure with increasing accuracy and precision, and explain degrees of trust in results.
